title: Approximate computation as satisfaction of the equality predicate
statement: Let $p$ be a private-coin protocol with randomness spaces $\Omega_X$ and $\Omega_Y$, input spaces $X$ and $Y$, and output type $\alpha$, each randomness space carrying a measure, let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a target function, and let $\varepsilon \in \bbr$. Then the proposition that $p$ approximately computes $f$ within error $\varepsilon$ coincides with the proposition that $p$ approximately satisfies, within error $\varepsilon$, the predicate that holds of $(x, y, a)$ exactly when $a = f(x, y)$.
hypotheses_covered: private-coin protocol p with randomness spaces Omega_X, Omega_Y and measures
target function f : X -> Y -> alpha
replaced:
For any private-coin protocol $p$, function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, and error bound
$\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
  p.\mathrm{ApproxComputes}\;f\;\varepsilon
  \;=\;
  p.\mathrm{ApproxSatisfies}\!\left(\lambda\,x\,y\,a,\; a = f\,x\,y\right)\varepsilon.
\]
In other words, $\varepsilon$-computing $f$ is the same as $\varepsilon$-satisfying the
equality predicate $a = f\,x\,y$.
